Night, torrential rain, a crowded wet Bengaluru street in 2047.

A BUSY PAVEMENT SEEN STRAIGHT ON. Fifteen or twenty ordinary Indian people of all ages, soaked
through, moving past camera under a concrete awning — hurrying, sheltering, carrying bags,
heads down against the rain. Everyone is wet, tired, unremarkable and unaware of the camera.

ONE FIGURE IN THE MIDDLE OF THEM IS STANDING COMPLETELY STILL AND LOOKING DIRECTLY AT CAMERA.

A man in his thirties in plain ordinary clothing. Entirely unremarkable. Not menacing, not
posed, not lit differently, not centred, not larger. AT A GLANCE HE IS JUST ANOTHER PERSON IN
THE CROWD. He is not a robot to look at — normal human skin, a normal human face.

THREE THINGS ARE WRONG AND NONE OF THEM IS OBVIOUS:

HE IS COMPLETELY DRY. His hair, his face and his clothing are not wet, in a street where every
other person is soaked and water is running off everyone.

HE IS PERFECTLY STILL while everyone around him is moving.

AND HE DOES NOT BLINK. Not once. His eyes stay open and level the entire time.

- - -
Live action, not a render. Documentary, straight on, medium-wide, at eye height. Long lens,
shallow depth — the crowd nearest and furthest are soft, he is sharp. RAIN MUST STREAK, NOT
DOT. Foreground rain crosses the lens. Droplets on the front element. Low dynamic range like
film — the sodium lamps clip to white, the deep street falls to true black. No global ambient
fill, no ambient-occlusion look. Genuine shadow noise, visible 35mm grain, chromatic
aberration, natural vignette.

Pore-level skin realism on everyone, including him. The crowd are real people — uneven,
ordinary, unposed.

COLOUR: dirty amber, wet grey, brown, oxide. Heavily desaturated, bleach-bypass, crushed
blacks. No teal, no cyan, no blue, no neon. No text or lettering.

A single machine, night, torrential rain, in a flooded street in 2047. No people.

A HEAVY DEMOLITION UNIT BUILT LIKE A BULL. Low, wide, enormously front-heavy, standing in
ankle-deep water facing camera. FOUR SHORT THICK LEGS with a wide stance and blunt wide feet.
Massive forward shoulders, all the mass in the front third, tapering to a narrow rear.

IT IS VISIBLY DAMAGED AND STILL WORKING. ONE SHOULDER IS CRUSHED IN AND HAS BEEN RE-PLATED —
three mismatched plates bolted over the dent in the wrong shade, weld beads unground, so that
shoulder sits lower than the other. It stands crooked because of it.

THE HEAD IS CLEARLY SEPARATE FROM THE SHOULDERS, thrust forward on a short heavy neck and
carried LOW, below shoulder height. IT HANGS SLIGHTLY CROOKED on a neck joint that no longer
centres. A blank battered plate where a face would be, with ONE THIN HORIZONTAL LIGHT LINE
across it, dim and flickering. NO horns, NO eyes, NO mouth.

MATERIAL: bare scored gunmetal and oxide alloy, deeply gouged across the front, rust blooming
from every weld and fixing. Chalked ochre stencils worn to metal. A panel missing from one
flank, exposing dry braided cabling and heavy pistons. Cable looms taped along the outside of
one leg.

IT IS STANDING COMPLETELY STILL WITH ITS HEAD DOWN, weight forward on the front legs.

BEHIND IT, A WALL WITH A HOLE PUNCHED THROUGH IT — masonry blown clean out, rubble in the
water, rebar bent outward.

- - -
Live action, not a render. Low camera, wide lens, close, so the shoulders loom. RAIN MUST
STREAK, NOT DOT. Foreground rain crosses the lens. Droplets on the front element. Low dynamic
range like film — sodium lamps clip to white, the deep street falls to true black. No global
ambient fill, no ambient-occlusion look. Genuine shadow noise, visible 35mm grain, chromatic
aberration, natural vignette.

ALL DAMAGE IS DRY. No fluid, nothing red.

desaturated, bleach-bypass, crushed blacks. No teal, no cyan, no blue, no neon. No text.

Night. Torrential rain. A vast field of scrapped machinery.

ON THE HIGHEST HEAD, VERY SMALL AGAINST IT, A HUMAN FIGURE.

THE FIGURE IS A PURE SILHOUETTE - solid black, no face, no features, no detail of any kind,
lit only from behind. It is a young male shape and nothing more.

THE POSE IS THE ENTIRE IMAGE - CLASSICAL KALIYA MARDANA:
ONE FOOT PLANTED FLAT on the crown of the highest head, weight fully on it.
THE OTHER LEG LIFTED HIGH AND CROSSED IN FRONT, knee bent, foot turned - a dance step, not
a fighting stance.
THE TORSO CURVED IN TRIBHANGA - the three bends, hips one way, chest the other, head the

ONE ARM RAISED HIGH ABOVE THE HEAD, holding up a long segmented length of the machine's own
tail, which trails away down behind and disappears into the mass.
THE OTHER ARM EXTENDED OUT AND SLIGHTLY DOWN for balance, hand loose.

THE FIGURE IS NOT STRAINING. NOTHING ABOUT THE POSE IS EFFORT. It is a dance performed on
top of something enormous, and that is what makes it frightening.

EVERYTHING ELSE IS NEARLY BLACK. The scrap field below is barely readable - shapes,

outfall wide enough to drive a bus into, half submerged, water pouring out of it. Everything

mouth of broken teeth.

into total darkness. A SINGLE THIN HORIZONTAL LIGHT LINE glows faintly far back inside it, dim
and unsteady.

have been crudely re-welded in place at the wrong angle.

THE CONCRETE HEADWALL IS SOAKED AND RUNNING WITH WATER. THE METAL INSIDE IS COMPLETELY DRY —
dusty, grey, unwetted. Rain and floodwater do not enter it. THAT CONTRAST IS THE TELL.

Twenty-five metres of segmented serpentine industrial units — the same chassis family as a sewer inspection serpent, the same identical machined segments, the same hinged armour plates, the same angular sensor heads — that have tangled in the same flooded drain for fifty years and CORRODED SOLID INTO EACH OTHER.

THE JOINS ARE RUST, NOT ENGINEERING. Where one body crosses another they have seized together, the gap between them filled with a thick crust of oxide and calcite. It is one mass now. Nobody built this. It accumulated.

THE BODY: a colossal braided trunk of dozens of interwoven segmented bodies, thicker than a car, twisting back on itself, with individual strands still readable within the mass. Loose ends of body trail out of it at intervals like severed cable.

THE HEADS: NINE NECKS rise from the mass at different heights and different angles, each ending in an angular armoured sensor head. THEY ARE NOT UNIFORM. Three are large and intact with their armour plates FULLY FLARED into wide cobra hoods. Two are smaller and half-flared. TWO ARE DEAD — hanging slack and inverted on limp necks, plates folded shut, dragging. One is crushed almost flat. One is missing its head entirely, the neck ending in a torn socket.

CONDITION: FIFTY YEARS UNDER WATER. Deep rust bleeding from every seam. Thick calcite bloom crusted along the undersides. Grey silt packed into every joint. Chalked yellow-grey paint surviving only in patches. Whole armour plates missing, others bent and crumpled. Dry cabling hanging in loops from breaks. POSTURE — THIS IS THE MAIN CHANGE. It is no longer standing upright with its arms open. - - - HOW IT IS PHOTOGRAPHED - - -

THIS IS A LIVE-ACTION VFX PLATE, NOT A RENDER. A real camera was carried into a real
flooded tunnel and pointed at real practical set pieces. Everything below describes the
physical behaviour of that camera.

CAMERA AND GLASS: ARRI ALEXA 35, ARRIRAW, 1/48th shutter at 24fps, wide open at T1.9 on
VINTAGE UNCOATED glass. LOW MICRO-CONTRAST, gentle highlight roll-off, soft rendering. The
glass is old and slightly hazy. NOT CLINICALLY SHARP ANYWHERE.

RAIN MUST STREAK, NOT DOT. Every falling drop is MOTION-BLURRED INTO A SOFT VERTICAL LINE by
the shutter. Streak lengths VARY WIDELY - long smears near the lamps, short ones in shadow.
The rain is NOT evenly distributed: it falls in GUSTS, CLUMPS AND SHEETS with visibly emptier
gaps between them, and drifts at a slight angle.

FOREGROUND RAIN CROSSES THE LENS. Several drops fall very close to the camera, far in front
of the focal plane, rendering as LARGE SOFT OUT-OF-FOCUS GREY SMEARS that cut vertically
across the frame and partially obscure what is behind them.

THE LENS IS DIRTY AND WET. Two or three water droplets sit ON THE FRONT ELEMENT itself,
静 and out of focus, smearing and refracting the lamps behind them into soft blobs. A faint
greasy smear across one corner. Fine dust and water spots.

DIRTY FLARE. The blown-out tunnel lamps throw STREAKED, ASYMMETRIC, IMPERFECT FLARE - not
clean geometric CG flare. Veiling glare washes milkily across the frame IMMEDIATELY AROUND
THE LAMPS ONLY, lifting the black there and nowhere else. Heavy HALATION BLOOM where every
highlight meets darkness.

THE SYMMETRY IS NOT PERFECT. The camera is very slightly off-axis and carries a SLIGHT ROLL
of one or two degrees. The left and right halves of the frame DO NOT MIRROR EXACTLY -
lighting, water, rust and coil placement differ noticeably side to side. It is handheld and
faintly unsteady.

FOCUS IS THIN AND SITS ON HER. Only the woman and the bundle are sharp. The nearest coils
are ALREADY SOFT. The hoods above are SOFT. The far tunnel dissolves into formless black.
THE FOREGROUND WATER IN THE BOTTOM OF FRAME IS HEAVILY OUT OF FOCUS.

SPECULAR BREAKUP - NOT UNIFORM GLOSS. The machines are NOT evenly wet and NOT evenly shiny.
Water runs in SHEETS down some plates while others are DRY, DULL, MATTE, CHALKY AND DUSTY.
Rust is rough and absorbs light. Only a few isolated wet edges catch a highlight. NO GLOBAL
SHEEN, NO PLASTIC GLOSS, NO UNIFORM WET LOOK, NO CLEAN REFLECTIVE SURFACES.

ATMOSPHERE: real airborne mist and spray thickening with distance. Contrast and saturation
FALL OFF STEEPLY into depth until the far tunnel is flat featureless grey-black murk.

LOW DYNAMIC RANGE, LIKE FILM, NOT LIKE A RENDER. NO GLOBAL AMBIENT FILL AND NO
AMBIENT-OCCLUSION LOOK. Anything not directly hit by a practical lamp falls to TRUE BLACK
WITH NO RECOVERABLE DETAIL. The lamps CLIP COMPLETELY TO PURE WHITE.

GRAIN AND NOISE: VISIBLE 35MM-SCALE GRAIN, COARSE AND IRREGULAR, HEAVIEST IN THE SHADOWS.
Genuine chroma noise in the darkest areas. SLIGHT CHROMATIC ABERRATION - magenta and green
fringing on high-contrast edges toward the frame corners. NATURAL LENS VIGNETTE.

THE SUBJECT: a decommissioned URBEX ROBOTICS UR-400 sewer inspection robot - a six-metre
segmented articulated serpentine machine, dead and abandoned for thirty years.

CONSTRUCTION: fifty or more IDENTICAL REPEATING MACHINED ALLOY SEGMENTS joined by exposed

ordered cabling run along the underside, clipped at regular intervals. Nothing tangled,

THE HEAD: a blunt angular armoured sensor housing, wider than the body, with a single

THE OBJECT: A TRANSVERSE BAMBOO FLUTE, about sixty centimetres long, a plain straight tube. It
reads unmistakably as a flute at a glance and in silhouette — no flare, no bell, no attachments
sticking out, nothing that changes its outline.

THE OUTER SHELL IS OLD BAMBOO. Dark, dry, hard, aged almost to brown-black, with visible nodes
and a worn polish where hands have held it. It has been used for a very long time.

BUT IT HAS BEEN REBUILT FROM THE INSIDE.

TWO LONG SPLITS RUN ALONG THE BAMBOO, one on each face, opened perhaps four millimetres wide
and running most of the length. THROUGH THE SPLITS, MACHINED METAL IS VISIBLE INSIDE — a
precision-turned sleeve of aged bronze and pale alloy, with fine concentric turning marks, tiny
milled ports and a row of minute hex fittings running along it. The engineering inside is far
finer than anything the outside suggests.

THE SPLITS ARE BOUND SHUT AT INTERVALS with fine dark wire, wrapped tight and twisted off, and
in two places with narrow strips of worn grey cloth. The repairs are handmade and not neat.

THE FINGER HOLES ARE NOT SIMPLE HOLES. Each one is a small MACHINED PORT set into the bamboo —
a bronze bezel with a fine mesh screen recessed inside it, precise and clean against the rough
wood around it. Six of them, unevenly spaced by hand.

THE MOUTHPIECE END: the blow hole is a machined bronze aperture with a knife-sharp edge. Just
behind it, a short SEALED BRONZE CHAMBER banded into the bamboo, with three minute apertures
around its circumference and one very fine dark seam.

THE FAR END: a plain bronze ferrule, worn smooth. Looking slightly into the bore, the inside is
lined with the same pale alloy sleeve, machined in fine rings.

ONE DETAIL THAT IS NOT LIKE THE OTHERS: a HAIRLINE FILAMENT runs the full length of the flute,
inlaid flush into the bamboo — barely a millimetre wide, and it does not look like metal, wood
or plastic. It catches light differently from everything around it, with a faint depth to it,
as though you are looking slightly into it rather than at it. It has no colour of its own.

IT DOES NOT GLOW. NOTHING ON THIS OBJECT EMITS LIGHT. There are no indicators, no readouts, no
buttons, no controls, no power source and no visible technology beyond the machining itself.

CONDITION: heavily used. Grime worked into the bamboo grain, a dark patina on the bronze,
oxidation greening in the recesses, one small dent in the ferrule, the binding wire dulled and
tarnished. It has been carried and played for years.

COLOUR: dark brown-black bamboo, aged bronze, pale alloy, dull grey wire, worn grey cloth.
Heavily desaturated and matte. No teal, no cyan, no blue, no neon, no bright colour.

ONE FOOT PLANTED FLAT on the crown of the highest head, weight fully on it.
THE OTHER LEG LIFTED HIGH AND CROSSED IN FRONT, knee bent, foot turned.
THE TORSO CURVED IN THREE BENDS — hips one way, chest the other, head the third. Fluid,

ONE ARM RAISED HIGH ABOVE THE HEAD, holding up a long segmented length of the machine's own
